title: This Bird Makes an Umbrella to Trick Fish
subject: black heron

scenes.text: This bird turns itself into an umbrella, and nobody agrees why.
It's the black heron, from southern Africa and Madagascar.
It stands in shallow water, tucks its head, and spreads its wings over its body like a canopy.
Some scientists think the shade cuts glare, like polarized sunglasses, so it can see fish.
Others think small fish swim into the shade looking for a place to hide.
It's called canopy feeding. It clearly works, and nobody has proved why.

description:
A bird that hunts by making an umbrella with its wings.
The black heron shades the water to hunt fish, and scientists still debate whether the shade helps it see, hide, or lure prey.
Why do you think it works?
first_comment: Shade to see, shade to hide, or shade to lure? Which theory do you pick?
